clue.text: One of a pair left, covered by a King: deceptive words!

parts.note: a doublet is one of a matching pair of things

indicators.note: covered by means the word left sits inside the following pieces

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A lone survivor of a pair, left under a king's protection, cries foul at the lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered by' puts L inside A + K, making ALK after DOUBLET.
explanation.definitionFit: Double-talk is evasive or misleading speech, so it is a fair synonym for deceptive words.

clue.text: Dish in Ibsen's house?

definitions.meaning: slang for an attractive person, a looker
Ibsen's play A ... House names its heroine's role; she is what lives in that house

explanation.definitionFit: A pretty woman is called a dish or a doll, and Ibsen's Nora is the doll of his play's title.

clue.text: Hoot Berg's femme fatale rising to make tea

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Lulu is the seductive heroine of Alban Berg's opera Lulu

indicators.note: make here means the letters of tea are made into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: An owlish cry as the opera's temptress gets up to brew a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns LULU into ULUL; 'make' rearranges TEA as ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ululate is to howl or wail, much as an owl hoots.

clue.text: Insurers' representative finds Jules's Strad broken, with a hole in it

indicators.note: in it means the hole is placed inside the rearranged letters
a broken violin is in pieces, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its possessive S counted as a letter
O is shaped like a hole

explanation.surface: A claims man discovers that Jules's Stradivarius has been smashed and holed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges JULESS + STRAD into LSSADJUSTER; 'in it' puts O after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss adjuster is the person an insurance company sends to assess a claim.

clue.text: Funds of store up

definitions.meaning: money or valuables held in reserve
to hoard or keep carefully as precious

explanation.definitionFit: Treasure is accumulated wealth, and as a verb it means to hoard or cherish.

clue.text: Literary Lambeth girl has a way to make a point in Cornwall

parts.note: Liza of Lambeth is Somerset Maugham's first novel; Lambeth is a district of London
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A London heroine from a novel finds her way to a Cornish headland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lizard is the headland at Britain's southernmost tip, in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: Lizard Point is a promontory, the most southerly in mainland Britain.

clue.text: Dislikable fellow, taking others' last taxi!

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of others'

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A rotter grabs the last taxi that others were waiting for.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is slang for a contemptible person, especially a strike-breaker.

clue.text: Instrument used with maps, perhaps, in Greek island?

indicators.note: in means the rearranged word goes inside the island's name

parts.note: Cos (or Kos) is an island in the Dodecanese

indicators.note: perhaps hints that maps is not the final form of these letters

explanation.surface: A navigational tool on an island in the Aegean, used alongside charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges MAPS to MPAS, which 'in' puts inside COS.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass is a navigational instrument read with charts.

clue.text: He hopes not to get chicken in the basket!

definitions.text: He hopes not to get chicken in the basket!

parts.words: He hopes not to get chicken in the basket!
parts.note: a man riding in the basket below a hot-air envelope hopes not to lose his nerve, with a nod to the pub dish chicken in a basket

explanation.surface: A diner dreading the pub menu's chicken-in-a-basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A balloon's crew rides in a basket and must not lose nerve aloft.

clue.text: Old coin to grab for decoration in the French style

parts.note: the louis d'or was an old French gold coin
to seize is to grab

explanation.surface: Snatching an antique coin to make an ornament in Gallic fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Seize names the ornamental style of Louis XVI's reign in France.

clue.text: Little woman left some alcohol

parts.note: Amy March is one of the sisters in Little Women

explanation.surface: A small lady departed, leaving a drop of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Amyl alcohol is a kind of solvent spirit, so the word names a type of alcohol.

clue.text: Shelf-life affected in Dorset shop

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Product durability is affected in a West Country shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelf-life' means life on the shelf, a spinster unmarried. Dorset is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: To be left on the shelf is to remain unmarried, the state of a single woman.

clue.text: Celebration for a recidivist, retiring

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: an old lag is a habitual criminal

explanation.surface: A party is thrown for a reformed old offender as he retires.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive occasion or special celebration.

clue.text: Dropping the subject of torture

parts.note: an old punishment in which the victim was hoisted by the wrists and let fall with a jerk

explanation.surface: Abandoning an unpleasant topic of conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Strappado was a torment of hauling a victim up by a rope and letting him drop.

clue.text: Flat-fish Authority, dare one say, has the skids under it!

parts.note: the skate is a flat ray-like fish
a board is a governing authority

explanation.surface: A fishery authority, one might say, is about to be sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dare one say' is a sly aside; 'has the skids under it' pretends to mean faces dismissal, but literally a board on wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: A skateboard is a plank mounted on wheels that runs under the rider.

clue.text: Reflex action of member being hammered

definitions.text: Reflex action of member being hammered

parts.words: Reflex action of member being hammered
parts.note: a doctor taps the leg joint with a small hammer and it kicks out involuntarily

explanation.surface: How a club member responds when he's beaten heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapping the patellar tendon makes the leg jolt involuntarily, the classic reflex test.

clue.text: Son taken in by wedding agreement

indicators.note: taken in by means the son is placed inside the wedding word

parts.note: a wedding is a union

explanation.surface: A boy is welcomed into the family by a marriage settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means in complete accord.

clue.text: Cave in mountain-pass, over fault

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a col is a pass between mountain peaks
a lapse is a slip or fault

explanation.surface: A cavern in a high pass, beyond a geological fault.
explanation.definitionFit: To cave in is to fall down or give way.

clue.text: Space-bar operator

parts.note: someone at a keyboard who works the long key for gaps, dressed up as a bartender in outer space

explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard worker strikes the space bar constantly.

clue.text: Hunt, possibly, for a bow-tie

definitions.meaning: William Holman Hunt, a Pre-Raphaelite artist, is an example
a rope at a boat's bow used to tie it up

explanation.walkthrough: 'bow-tie' is not neckwear: the bow is a boat's front.
explanation.definitionFit: Holman Hunt was an artist, and a painter is also a mooring line fastened at a boat's bow.

clue.text: Vessel docked at Mersey port in vain

indicators.note: docked at means the vessel is placed beside the port

parts.note: Bootle is a dock town on the Mersey beside Liverpool
SS is a steamship

explanation.surface: A ship ties up at a Liverpool dock, all for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootless is an old word for useless or unavailing.

clue.text: National side on the ball in America

definitions.meaning: belonging to a nation, here England

definitions.text: side on the ball in America
definitions.meaning: Americans call the spin put on a billiard or pool ball this

explanation.definitionFit: English is England's national language, and US pool players call sidespin english.

clue.text: Journey routed a new way

indicators.note: a new way says the letters of routed are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trip that was redirected along another route.
explanation.definitionFit: A detour is a roundabout journey.

clue.text: Wider bell forged to make a stir

indicators.note: forged means hammered into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Casting a broader bell to create a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridewell, a London jail, became a general word for a prison; 'stir' is slang for prison, not a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is slang for prison, and a bridewell is an old term for a jail.

clue.text: Rowdy celebration with a piece of Indian music

parts.note: a rag is a boisterous student festival or prank

explanation.surface: A noisy party with some Indian music playing.
explanation.definitionFit: A raga is a melodic framework in Indian classical music.

clue.text: Field poppy's head seen in spring

parts.note: a lea is a meadow

indicators.note: head points to the first letter of poppy's

explanation.surface: The top of a poppy shows in a meadow in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring is to jump or bound.

clue.text: Voice contributing to unusual tone

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A singer adds to an odd sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Alto is a singing voice range, lower than soprano.

clue.text: Cartoonist no longer drawing is in a position to avoid publicity

parts.note: David Low, the political cartoonist, had died, so no longer at work
a profile is a side-view drawing

explanation.surface: A retired cartoonist keeps out of the limelight.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a low profile means staying unobtrusive and out of the news.

clue.text: Head of darning-needle used as dagger

indicators.note: head of points to the first letter of darning

parts.note: to needle is to irritate or irk

explanation.surface: The tip of a sewing needle serves as a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirk is a Scottish short stabbing blade.

clue.text: Half-day closing craft alliance

indicators.note: half takes the first three of the day's six letters

parts.note: Friday is a day of the week
an end is a closing
a ship is a vessel or craft

explanation.surface: Shops shutting early one day makes for a boat alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-day closing was the old British custom of shops shutting one afternoon a week.
explanation.definitionFit: A friendship is a bond of mutual support, like an alliance.
